html:
SMTO-DB-0010 — The database reported an error while SMTO was using it

GUID: 5242e67f-7fa2-4020-948d-dfb2e78b0fa2
Slug: database-client-failed
Domain: DB · Subsystem: db

What happened

  • The database program SMTO uses reported a problem, such as being unable to connect, wrong sign-in details, missing permission, or a mistake in the query. If SMTO was changing data, part of that change may already have happened.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If SMTO was changing data, ask it to only look at the affected rows, for example "Show me order 1042 without changing anything". Only ask for the change again if it isn't there. The failure may have come after part of the change was made, and repeating it could apply it twice.
  2. Open Technical details in this panel and read the database's message, such as "password authentication failed", "could not connect" or "permission denied". That message names the real cause, which decides which of the next fixes applies.
  3. For sign-in or connection messages, open Parameter Store, select the database entry and check its host, port, database name, user and password on the Value tab. A wrong address or password stops the database from accepting SMTO's connection.
  4. Make sure the database server is running and reachable from the computer running the Gateway (the helper program SMTO uses to run commands). See Settings › Setup › Gateways. SMTO connects to the database from the Gateway's computer, not from your browser.

What success looks like

  • SMTO returns database results, and for changes, a read-only check shows the change exactly once.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO or the database. Don't ask SMTO to repeat a change until you've confirmed it didn't already happen.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The psql client run through the Gateway exited with a nonzero status (or discovery returned connection_failed); its sanitized stderr is reported as the database error, and whether any change took effect is not established.

What this means

  • The dispatched psql process reports a nonzero exit_code and its captured diagnostic is returned as the database error. Input rejection is pre-dispatch only where the producer says so. Discovery and psql failures require their original execution evidence; diagnostics do not run SQL or prove that a mutation rolled back.

Why this can happen

  • The dispatched psql process reports a nonzero exit_code and its captured diagnostic is returned as the database error.

How to diagnose it

  • Examine bounded stderr, exit status and transaction evidence for the original statement and target.

How to fix it

  • Read the psql stderr in Technical details to separate connection, authentication, permission and SQL errors, and check that psql is installed on the executing Gateway and can reach the host:port. For any write, inspect the target rows and transaction state before resubmitting; a nonzero exit does not prove a rollback, and an outcome_unknown status means delivery itself is unconfirmed. Never blindly repeat the statement.
  • Inspect the bounded database diagnostics for the actual connection, permission or SQL cause. For mutations, inspect transaction/target state before repeating the statement.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect and reconcile authoritative state before repeating a mutation. Do not blindly retry.

How to verify the fix

  • The specific client/database cause is resolved and mutation state is reconciled before another submission.

What not to do

  • Do not repeat a mutation while the earlier outcome or current owner is unresolved.

Technical notes

  • Input rejection is pre-dispatch only where the producer says so. Discovery and psql failures require their original execution evidence; diagnostics do not run SQL or prove that a mutation rolled back.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
